content:
Written by Matt Schorr

Clarksville, TN – Adams is a quiet little town in Robertson County, just twenty miles east of Clarksville. By the latest census count, only 624 residents call it home, and by all appearances, it’s the sort of place you might think time forgot. There are winding roads and peaceful countrysides, expansive farmland and rustic homes. In many ways, it’s a setting pulled from an episode of The Andy Griffith Show.

But there’s a dark spot in the history of Adams, a dark spot with tendrils that reach across the centuries like an ancient eldritch horror. Tales of otherworldly creatures, unexplainable happenings, and disturbing horrors linger there, bringing an unsettling dread to the area when night falls and settles over the land like a dark blanket.

…if you believe in such things…

This is the story of the Bell Witch, one of America’s most infamous hauntings. The legend has drawn historians, ghost hunters, and seekers of the supernatural from every corner of the world for several generations. (Type it into Google or YouTube, and you’ll get a library of content from bloggers, vloggers, and self-proclaimed paranormal experts.)

The specter at the heart of the fervor is a ghost that’s haunted the area for centuries, a wraith responsible for prophecies, violence, and – according to the legends – murder. This is its story.

…if you believe in such things…

Mysterious Beginning

The story begins in 1817.

John Bell, a successful plantation farmer, happened upon a strange animal while checking his cornfields in what was then the Red River Community. According to accounts gathered over time, the animal had the body of a dog and the head of a rabbit. It sat in the middle of a corn row, regarding John with a quiet gaze.

How long John, then 67 years old, stared back at the animal before raising his gun to fire at it, no one knows. Likewise, there’s no official record indicating if his actions were to simply drive away an intrusive critter or the result of genuine fear.

Whatever the case, John’s numerous gunshots didn’t slay the creature. They missed it entirely, and then it disappeared.

Sometime later, a slave the family owned, whose name was Dean, reported a large, black dog would follow him home on evenings when he visited his wife. The dog, Dean said, sometimes had two heads.

Dean soon began carrying a “witch ball,” a charm traditionally used to ward off evil spirits. His wife created it to protect him.

John’s son, Drewry, who was 20 at the time, encountered an unknown bird perched on a fence that lined the property. Drewry said the bird’s size was extraordinary, and it flew away when he approached it.

Meanwhile, Betsy, the youngest daughter, met a mysterious girl in a green dress on the property. The girl was swinging and playing on the limb of an old oak tree. Whatever came of that encounter is open to speculation.

…if you believe in such things…

The Haunting Commences

The paranormal activity wasn’t content to remain in the fields, though.

On the evening of John’s encounter with the dog-like creature, the family gathered for what was, no doubt, a traditional family dinner. A rustic, wooden table. A full spread of plates.
A family of ten breaking bread and recounting their respective days.

The sort of visual you might expect in an old Western.

This was interrupted, however, by strange thumping sounds outside, like something was beating against the walls of their log home. Something big. Deep, solid thuds halted all dinner conversation.

Perhaps the home itself even creaked and groaned beneath the repeated impacts. We can only guess.

John and his sons – Jesse, John, Jr., Drewry, and Zadok – rushed out to catch the intruder. The youngest sons, Richard and Joel, likely remained inside with their sisters, Esther and Betsy, and their mother, Lucy.

With lanterns at the ready – and perhaps even a rifle or two – the men raced outside. Once there, however, they found no one. The nearby woods were empty. The grounds were quiet. But not for long.

In the nights that followed, the thumping sounds returned. They grew louder and more frequent, reaching chaotic fever pitches, interrupting both meals and sleep as an unseen being thrashed against the home without mercy. Each night, John and his boys rushed to investigate, and each night, they returned empty-handed.

The Entity Targets the Children

Then, the activity moved indoors.

Weeks later, the Bell children woke their parents at night, several of them frightened and crying. There were rats in their room, they insisted. Dozens of them. All gnawing at their beds in the dark.

The family never found any sign of such rodents, but the children insisted rats were chewing on their bedposts while they slept. Rapid, rhythmic scratching and faint crunching noises filled the children’s ears, leaving them worried their beds might collapse at any moment.

This was soon accompanied by more disturbing noises. The distinct, metallic rattle of chains being dragged across the floor were heard. Scraping, sharp rattles as metallic links struck one another, joined by heavy thuds on the hardwood.

But no chains were found, nor any intruder carrying them.

Then, the family overheard what sounded like dogs fighting outside in the night. Low, hard, and angry growls rang out, along with sharp snaps and high-pitched, frantic snarls, followed by breathless panting and furious rumbles.

When investigated, of course, no dogs were ever discovered. No tracks. No fur.

Nothing.

Escalation and Sadism

The entity’s action then escalated. No longer satisfied with simple bullying, it grew sadistic and cruel.

Once more, John and Lucy were awakened by their children’s cries at night. Something, the children insisted, was pulling their blankets from them while in bed. Something they couldn’t see. Something … ghostly.

This unseen force also took hold of their pillows while they slept. It then yanked the pillows from under the children’s heads and tossed them to the floor.

As before, there were no tracks – human or otherwise – leading into or out of the house during these incidents. The intruder left no sign of its presence, apart from its cruelty.

…if you believe in such things…

We’ll continue the Bell Witch’s tale in the next edition of Clarksville Living, which will include the entity declaring its name, how it targeted specific members of the Bell family, and a confrontation with the would-be U.S. President Andrew Jackson.
